penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Building a middleware or managed package that injects tracking parameters into SFMC distributed content blocks requires bespoke implementation work per client environment — SFMC org structure, sandbox access, and AMPscript/SSJS configuration vary significantly across enterprise accounts. Delivery is not a self-serve automated flow.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Enterprise SFMC customers expect scoped discovery calls, IT/security review, and guided onboarding before any middleware touches their production email sends. This is not a self-serve signup-and-go product.

rationale: The buyer is real and well-funded — marketing ops leads at enterprises already paying five-to-six figures annually for SFMC — and the pain is a documented platform limitation confirmed by Salesforce support, so willingness to pay is credible. However, the solution is a technical middleware or managed package that must be implemented inside each client's SFMC org, which requires per-customer hands-on work (AMPscript/SSJS, connector setup, security review) that Claude and a simple landing page cannot automate. Operational autonomy scores critically low (3), and buildability with AI scores low (3) because this is not a prompt-plus-Stripe product — it is a platform integration requiring enterprise-grade implementation. Both are hard build-gate failures, and penalties for human fulfillment and synchronous sales push the total to 2.3, well below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: This idea is not viable for a solo non-technical operator running this Claude factory. The 'product' would need to reach inside each client's Salesforce Marketing Cloud org, modify AMPscript or SSJS content-block logic, and potentially require Salesforce ISV certification or a managed package — none of which can be built or delivered without deep SFMC technical expertise and per-customer implementation work. Even if a consultant could build a v1 tool, selling it would require enterprise sales cycles with security reviews and IT approvals. There is no realistic self-serve, automated, prompt-based version of this. The factory should drop this candidate and flag the underlying insight — SFMC distributed tracking gaps — only if a genuinely automatable wrapper (e.g. a UTM-appending pre-send webhook that requires no SFMC org access) becomes plausible with new SFMC API capabilities.
notes: Failing build gates: operational_autonomy (scored 3, minimum 7) and buildability_with_ai (scored 3, minimum 6). The core constraint is architectural: any real fix lives inside the client's SFMC org and requires platform-level access and configuration that cannot be abstracted into a self-serve Claude-powered micro-service. Drop unless a lightweight, org-agnostic angle (e.g. a pre-send URL-wrapping API that teams paste into their blocks manually) can be validated as genuinely self-serve.
